key_insight: An interpretable AI model predicted 12-month liver cancer risk in people with cirrhosis better than two established risk scores while separately modeling competing death or transplantation.
clinical_relevance: The model could support research into risk-tailored hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance, but this study does not establish improved patient outcomes.
method: Used regional routine health data from 17,177 adults with cirrhosis in Andalusia.
Trained an Explainable Boosting Machine using demographics, diagnosis codes and eight routine laboratory tests.
Predicted HCC, death or transplantation without HCC, or no event over 12 months.
evidence_signal: Across 20 repeats of 5-fold cross-validation, HCC AUROC was 0.734; at routine encounters, time-dependent AUC exceeded aMAP (0.790 vs 0.688) and the Toronto HCC Risk Index (0.761 vs 0.703).
watch_item: Evidence comes from one Spanish region; prospective validation elsewhere is needed before clinical implementation, and this is risk-prediction research rather than drug discovery.
paper_title: Interpretable competing-risk prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma in cirrhosis from region-wide routine health data
